title: interstage-sampler-fusion-and-deferred-decode-windowing
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: continuous-batching and prefill/decode handoff currently incur repeated kernel launches and buffer materialization when sampling decisions are resolved only during decode. This PR introduces two cooperating mechanisms to reduce kernel churn and KV cache thrash: 1) an Interstage Sampler component that computes lightweight sampling hints during prefill and encodes them into a compact hint payload attached to the request context, and 2) Deferred Decode Windowing which groups decode invocations into micro-windows that allow the scheduler to fuse compatible kernels and coalesce KV cache accesses. The changes reduce per-request kernel launches and improve GPU kernel occupancy for medium-length generations.

What changed (high level): implemented an interstage sampler interface in the serving runtime, added a hint-serialization path that travels with the request through scheduler and executor layers, extended the scheduler to recognize hint-aligned requests and opportunistically perform in-place sampling decisions during prefill-to-decode handoff, and introduced a deferred-decode windowing policy that batches short decodes into micro-windows of configurable time/size thresholds. Also added a soft-locking mechanism for KV cache entries to avoid immediate eviction when a prefill indicates imminent reuse. The implementation is careful to keep the public API unchanged; all behavior is guarded by a feature flag (runtime.experimental.interstage_sampler) and rollout knobs (window_size_ms, max_window_tokens).

Design notes: the interstage sampler emits one of three hint classes (greedy, topk-k-prob, temperature-sample-metadata) encoded as a compact enum+payload to avoid bloating network buffers. Deferred windows are sized to prioritize throughput gains while bounding added per-token latency; defaults are 6ms or 8 tokens whichever first. Scheduler-level changes include a kernel fusion planner that merges prefetched logits with decode kernels when hints are compatible, and a KV soft-lock counter with TTL to prevent eviction during immediate handoffs. The approach is conservative by default and falls back to existing prefill/decode handoff semantics if hints are missing or incompatible.

Compatibility and safety: feature-flagged rollout, end-to-end regression tests added (unit + integration + nightly perf suite). KV soft-locks use a bounded counter to avoid permanent leakage; the soft-lock acquires only when prefill declares reuse within the configured horizon. The feature is disabled in Dedicated beta clusters until we've validated SLA impacts.

Benchmarks (summary): measured on v100-equivalent cluster with mixed short/medium workloads: +9-12% aggregate throughput for mixed traffic, ~20% fewer kernel launches per request, 7% lower GPU memory churn during bursts, and median latency unchanged. 99th percentile for tiny single-token generations increased by 1.8–6ms in the worst-case windowing configuration; default windows keep increase under 3ms which is within our latency SLO for non-low-latency tiers.

review_conversation: Kelsey Nguyen: Can you clarify how hints are validated across model variants? Reply: Interstage sampler encodes model-agnostic hint classes and includes a small compatibility vector. Scheduler validates hint/model pair before fusion; incompatible hints are ignored.

Ravi Sharma: Concern about 99p latency regressions for single-token completions. Reply: We added a strict default (6ms / 8 tokens) and a new 'low-latency' runtime profile disables windowing. Also included regression tests and observed <3ms increase in default config.
Marta Lopez: Request to add observability for hint hit/miss rate. Reply: Added metrics runtime.interstage.hints.{emitted,used,ignored,invalid} and dashboard panels in the PR.
Kelsey Nguyen: nit: move TTL constant to config; resolved in a follow-up commit.
Ravi Sharma: approved after seeing perf numbers and added tests.
benchmarks_summary: Mixed workload on 4xA100-like nodes: aggregate throughput +9-12%, kernel launches per request -20%, GPU memory churn -7%. Median latency stable; 99th for tiny requests +1.8–3.0ms on default windowing, configurable via runtime_profile.
rollout_plan: Gate behind runtime.experimental.interstage_sampler flag; staged rollout to canary cluster (5% traffic) for 48h, monitor runtime.interstage.hints.used, scheduler.fused_kernels, cpu/gpu utilization, and p99 latency. If no regressions, ramp to 25% then 100% over a week. Dedicated customers will have feature disabled by default and can opt-in.
release_notes: Introduce experimental interstage sampler and deferred decode windowing to reduce kernel churn and improve throughput. Defaulted off for Dedicated; rollout controlled by runtime.experimental.interstage_sampler. Performance improvements for mixed workloads; minor tail-latency implications for extremely short-lived requests.
